standard_prerequisites.name: Signed tableau rules for disjunction
standard_prerequisites.statement: From True (A or B) the True-or rule branches into True A and True B; from False (A or B) the False-or rule adds both False A and False B to the same branch.
standard_prerequisites.use: Item (1) closes via the True-or split against the derived False A and False B; item (2) closes via the False-or conclusions against the True assumptions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Inconsistency via closed tableaux
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set of sentences is inconsistent iff some finite subset has a closed tableau.
standard_prerequisites.use: Item (1) is witnessed by a closed tableau for the signed assumption set {True (A or B), True (not A), True (not B)}.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1107-1112): (1) {A or B, not A, not B} is inconsistent; (2) both A proves A or B and B proves A or B.

Item (1) (proof lines 1114-1132): a closed tableau for {True (A or B), True (not A), True (not B)}: the True-not rules derive False A and False B, then the True-or rule on the root splits; the True A branch closes against False A and the True B branch closes against False B.

Item (2) (proof lines 1133-1153): closed tableaux for {False (A or B), True A} and for {False (A or B), True B}: the False-or rule derives False A and False B on the branch, which closes because False A contradicts the assumption True A (resp. False B contradicts True B).
proof_roadmap: Witness item (1) with the three-assumption closed tableau split by True-or.
Witness item (2) with the two False-or tableaux against each True assumption.
Both items deliver closed trees, so the stated derivability and inconsistency facts hold.
